clue.text: Miss appointment with firm — an average joker

parts.note: to stand someone up is to miss a date with them
CO is the abbreviation for company, a firm
the median is a kind of average

explanation.surface: Someone who skips a meeting with a company is dismissed as a run-of-the-mill clown.
explanation.walkthrough: 'An average joker' reads as one phrase, but 'average' belongs to the wordplay and 'joker' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A comic who performs standing before a live audience is a professional joker.

clue.text: Attire for the Lido with roughly two GCSEs, minimum

indicators.note: roughly means put together crudely, so the letters of the following words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A pupil needs at least a couple of GCSEs to get kitted out for the pool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'roughly' rearranges the letters of TWO GCSES MINIMUM. A lido is an open-air public swimming pool in Britain; GCSEs are the exams English pupils sit at sixteen.
explanation.definitionFit: The garment worn for bathing at an outdoor pool is a one-piece swimsuit.

clue.text: Vauxhall model almost off course

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: astray means off course, wandering from the route

explanation.surface: A particular Vauxhall car has nearly gone off the road.
explanation.definitionFit: The Astra is a long-running family hatchback made by the British car brand Vauxhall.

clue.text: Chinatown

parts.note: read as china town: a town famous for its porcelain

explanation.walkthrough: The word suggests the Chinese quarter of a city, or the Polanski film; split it and it asks for a town that gives its name to china.
explanation.definitionFit: The German city is famous for the porcelain sold under its name, so it is a town of china.

clue.text: Publicity broadcast that is plain

parts.note: PR stands for public relations, publicity
to air something is to broadcast it
i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, that is

explanation.surface: An advertisement goes out on air that is simple and unadorned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plain' looks like an adjective in the surface; it is the noun for flat grassland.
explanation.definitionFit: A wide expanse of flat grassland is a plain, especially in North America.

clue.text: Bunting seen from floor to landing

indicators.note: the answer can be seen within the run of letters that follows

parts.note: the letters run across flOOR TO LANding

explanation.surface: Decorative flags are strung up from the ground floor to the top of the stairs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'seen from' signals that the answer sits inside 'floor to landing'. 'Bunting' suggests party flags; here it is the bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The ortolan is a small European songbird of the bunting family, once a delicacy.

clue.text: Walford resident's caught strange body part

parts.note: Walford is the East London borough of the soap EastEnders; a Cockney there drops the H from heard, which means caught
rum is British slang for odd or strange

explanation.surface: Someone from the EastEnders set has picked up an odd anatomical ailment.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockney speech drops initial H, so 'heard' (caught, as in caught what was said) becomes EARD.
explanation.definitionFit: The tympanic membrane inside the ear is a part of the human body.

clue.text: Artiste away from Barking industrial estate, protected from the elements

indicators.note: barking means mad, so the letters are scrambled; it also poses as the East London district

explanation.surface: A performer leaves an industrial park in the London suburb of Barking, sheltered from the weather.
explanation.walkthrough: Barking is a place in East London, which makes 'Barking industrial estate' look like an address. Take the letters of ARTISTE away from INDUSTRIALESTATE and rearrange what is left.
explanation.definitionFit: Something wrapped in a layer that keeps out cold, heat or damp has been shielded against the weather.

clue.text: Nightmare on this broadcast showing county

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered widely, so these letters are spread about into a new order

explanation.surface: A horror show screened on television reveals a part of England.
explanation.definitionFit: It is an English shire in the East Midlands, home of Robin Hood's Sherwood.

clue.text: Patients treated outside hospital way back when

indicators.note: outside means surrounding, so the rearranged letters go around the hospital abbreviation
treated means processed or worked on, so the letters are reworked

parts.note: H is the map abbreviation for hospital

explanation.surface: Patients were once cared for outside a hospital, long ago.
explanation.walkthrough: 'treated' rearranges PATIENTS into INTEPAST, and 'outside' puts that around H for hospital, split after INT.
explanation.definitionFit: Both phrases refer to an earlier time that has gone by, in former days.

clue.text: Inhabitant has no den to take exams again

indicators.note: has no means lacks, so these letters are taken out

parts.note: a resident is an inhabitant

explanation.surface: A tenant without a study has to sit the tests a second time.
explanation.definitionFit: To sit a failed examination a second time is to resit it in British schools.

clue.text: Wind knocked over communist base first

indicators.note: first means the base word comes at the front

parts.note: base means mean, low or ignoble

indicators.note: knocked over means turned upside down, so in an across answer the word is read backwards

parts.note: RED is a common word for a communist

explanation.surface: A gust floors a Marxist after first hitting their foundations.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knocked over' turns RED into DER, and 'first' puts MEAN (base) in front. 'Wind' reads as moving air; it is the verb, rhyming with find.
explanation.definitionFit: A river that winds follows a twisting, looping course, which is to meander.

clue.text: Vegans left Seville orange squashed on Rhine rock

indicators.note: squashed means crushed out of shape, so the letters are rearranged once the others have gone

explanation.surface: Vegans left a crushed bitter orange on a German river crag.
explanation.walkthrough: 'left' asks for the letters of VEGANS to be removed from SEVILLE ORANGE, and 'squashed' rearranges the remaining EILLEOR.
explanation.definitionFit: The Lorelei is a famous steep slate cliff above the river at St Goarshausen, linked with a siren legend.

clue.text: Windbag occasionally presents royal occupant of Castle Adamant?

indicators.note: occasionally means now and then, so only every other letter is taken

parts.note: the second, fourth and sixth letters of wInDbAg

explanation.surface: A boaster sometimes introduces the princess who lives in a fortress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'occasionally' takes every other letter of Windbag, starting with the second. Castle Adamant is the women's university in Gilbert and Sullivan's comic opera Princess Ida.
explanation.definitionFit: The title heroine of the Gilbert and Sullivan opera is a princess who presides over Castle Adamant.

clue.text: Native American drops third note to one who's proposed

indicators.note: drops means lets go of, so these letters are removed

parts.note: the Menominee are a Native American people of Wisconsin
me (mi) is the third note of the sol-fa scale do, re, me

explanation.surface: A tribesman lets fall a musical note to a suitor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drops' removes ME, the third sol-fa note, from MENOMINEE. 'one who's proposed' suggests a suitor; it means a candidate put forward.
explanation.definitionFit: A candidate who has been put forward for a post or award has been named by someone.

clue.text: Spread grain out, eaten by horse

indicators.note: eaten by means swallowed inside, so the rearranged letters go within the other word

parts.note: a mare is a female horse

indicators.note: out means put out of order, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: Seed is scattered and gobbled up by a horse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges GRAIN into GARIN, and 'eaten by' puts that inside MARE, between MAR and E. 'Spread' looks like a verb; it is the noun for something put on bread.
explanation.definitionFit: Margarine is a butter substitute that is smeared on toast, a classic spread.

clue.text: Length of US railroad

parts.note: an el is an elevated railway in American cities, such as Chicago's

explanation.surface: Someone asks how long an American railway line runs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Length' is both the definition of the old cloth measure and the L tacked on to EL, the American elevated railway; 'of' joins them.
explanation.definitionFit: An ell is an old measure of cloth, about forty-five inches long.

clue.text: ID in magenta looking odd

indicators.note: looking odd means appearing strange or out of shape, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An identity card printed in purplish red looks peculiar.
explanation.definitionFit: A label worn on the chest showing who you are serves as identification.

clue.text: Fairbrother's tune

indicators.note: the possessive reads as has: the name has the answer inside it

parts.note: the letters sit inside fAIRbrother

explanation.surface: A melody composed by someone named Fairbrother.
explanation.definitionFit: An air is a simple melody or song.

clue.text: Blimey, Alec capsized the boat

parts.note: cor is a British exclamation of surprise, like blimey

indicators.note: capsized means overturned and tumbled about, so the letters of the name are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone exclaims in shock that Alec has turned the boat over.
explanation.definitionFit: A coracle is a small round Welsh boat made of wicker covered with hide.

clue.text: Cannot even eat here!

parts.note: can't is the contraction of cannot
e'en is the poetic contraction of even

explanation.surface: An exasperated cry that a place is not even fit to dine in.
explanation.definitionFit: A canteen is a dining room at a workplace or school where people take meals.

clue.text: Husband in lean-to brewing alcohol

indicators.note: in means the letter goes inside the rearranged ones
brewing means being mixed up and fermented, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A man makes home brew in a garden shed.
explanation.definitionFit: Ethanol is the chemical name for the intoxicant in beer, wine and spirits.

clue.text: Dignified to a degree, relatively speaking?

definitions.note: this definition is a noun phrase in disguise: speaking in terms of relatives, the answer is one

parts.note: grand means stately and dignified
an MA, Master of Arts, is a university degree

explanation.surface: Someone is stately up to a point, comparatively speaking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to a degree' reads as somewhat, but 'to' only links and 'a degree' supplies the MA.
explanation.definitionFit: A grandmother is a family relation, so in kinship terms she is a relative.

clue.text: Achieved success — after many miles?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to have ... is to have done well in life
second meaning: literally, having travelled a long distance

explanation.walkthrough: The dash makes it read as a long road to success; the phrase works both figuratively and literally.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for a successful career is the same as the literal phrase for a long journey.

clue.text: Rough road ran somewhere up in the Pyrenees

indicators.note: rough means unrefined or disordered, so the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: A bumpy mountain track ran to a high spot in the Pyrenees.
explanation.definitionFit: Andorra is a tiny principality high in the mountains between France and Spain.

clue.text: Tango with a pair of ducks, also

parts.note: Tango is T in the NATO phonetic alphabet
a duck is a zero score in cricket, shaped like O, so two of them are OO

explanation.surface: Someone dances a tango with two ducks as well.
explanation.definitionFit: Too means as well, in addition.

clue.text: Watertight floodgate

definitions.meaning: first meaning: sound and watertight, as of a ship
second meaning: a ... (stanch) is an old word for a floodgate or weir that holds water back

explanation.walkthrough: Read together it sounds like a description of a sluice; the two words are separate meanings, the second a rare noun.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes a hull that keeps water out; the archaic noun is a barrier that stems a flow.

clue.text: When interviewers show agreement with seabirds

definitions.meaning: first meaning: TV cutaway shots of an interviewer nodding

explanation.walkthrough: 'with' joins the two meanings. In television jargon, a noddy is a reaction shot filmed after an interview.
explanation.definitionFit: The broadcasting term and the name of a tern species are the same plural noun.

clue.text: An unexpected bonus on a cake!

definitions.text: An unexpected bonus on a cake!

parts.words: An unexpected bonus on a cake!
parts.note: plays on the idiom for an extra pleasing touch, and the sugary topping literally on a cake

explanation.walkthrough: The idiom 'the ... on the cake' means a bonus on top of something already good; the literal topping is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The sweet sugar coating spread on top of a cake is the extra treat in the idiom.

clue.text: 'TU' — there's a French article about it

indicators.note: about means around, so the article goes around the other word

parts.note: une is the French feminine indefinite article, a

explanation.surface: Someone notes that a French grammar text has a piece on the pronoun tu.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts UNE around IT. 'TU' looks like the French for you; it is the abbreviation of trade union, and Unite is Britain's big union.
explanation.definitionFit: Unite is the name of one of the largest British labour organisations, a trade union.

clue.text: First lieutenant dropping sultan round for Pharaoh queen

indicators.note: round means turned about, so the leftover letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A senior officer leaves a sultan behind and turns to a royal Egyptian.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dropping sultan' removes the letters of SULTAN from FIRST LIEUTENANT, and 'round' rearranges the remaining FIRIETENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Nefertiti was the wife of the Egyptian ruler Akhenaten, a famous queen.

clue.text: Constant that's instrumental in marriage break-ups?

definitions.note: a plural noun phrase for a singular answer: the situation that causes them

parts.note: eternal means constant, unending
a triangle is a percussion instrument

explanation.surface: A permanent factor plays a part in couples splitting up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'instrumental in' reads as responsible for; 'instrumental' gives the musical instrument and 'in' links to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A love affair involving two lovers and a spouse is a classic cause of divorce.
